steps.title: Lock the Edge product scope and migration plan
steps.summary: Confirm the year-one product outcomes, prioritised backlog and migration approach for the current King’s Edge platform. Define the minimum live service to preserve, the richer activity model needed for events, self-paced activity, projects and sustained experiences, the priority management and evidence workflows, the in-house digital-badging scope, the bounded King’s Canvas prototype, and the data, operational and content responsibilities that Edge must supply to the development team. Begin this work as the core multidisciplinary team becomes available during November 2026 and complete the product and migration definition by the end of February 2027.

steps.title: Replatform the core Edge service into Azure
steps.summary: Move the current Edge platform onto the shared Azure stack while maintaining continuity for live delivery. Rebuild and migrate the essential opportunity catalogue, search and discovery, registration, attendance and participation records, cohort restrictions and targeted curation, activity-owner administration, communications, reporting, audit trails and relevant historical data. Establish the flexible opportunity and experience model that later releases will use, and align the shopfront with 1.2 Data Foundations and Student Systems.

steps.title: Deliver in-house digital badging and retire Accredible
steps.summary: Run digital badging as a dedicated deadline-led workstream in parallel with the wider Edge replatform. Deliver badge definition and metadata, issuer and administrator roles, automatic and manual issuance, verified self-claim and off-platform recognition routes, student display, public verification, audit, revocation, reporting and support arrangements. Migrate the required issuers, badge definitions and credential records from Accredible, validate service continuity and complete cutover by the end of August 2027 so the existing subscription can be stood down before the September renewal point.

steps.title: Put projects and King’s Canvas into controlled use
steps.summary: Release the priority capabilities that extend Edge beyond event booking into projects and wider experiences, drawing from milestones, progress tracking, resource hosting, groups, submissions, outputs, collections, pathways, provider curation, self-paced experiences and participant communications according to backlog priority. Introduce student self-claim and evidence upload and staff verification workflows where these are not already delivered through the badging workstream. Test a saved and revisitable King’s Canvas prototype that lets students map needs and aspirations, receive bounded AI coaching and connect their thinking to relevant opportunities.

steps.title: Launch the connected Edge-led Hub kernel
steps.summary: Bring the migrated core Edge service, project and experience management, evidence, the in-house digital-badging service and the agreed Canvas prototype into one coherent student experience. Complete accessibility, security, performance, analytics, documentation, support and operational ownership for the live Edge-led kernel of the Student Experience Hub, while retaining the separate August 2027 deadline for Accredible exit.

steps.title: Connect planning, opportunity, participation, evidence and recognition
steps.summary: Use evidence from year-one operation to strengthen the connected Edge journey. Improve movement from Canvas needs and aspirations into relevant opportunities, connect activity progress and completion to evidence and recognition, introduce proportionate post-activity reflection, and mature collections or pathways where they help students progress from lighter-touch to deeper experiences. Develop recognition in response to the proposition led by 2.4.3 Enhanced Academic Transcript, with 2.1.3 and 2.2.3 supplying the skills, governance and assurance inputs it requires.

steps.title: Move Edge fully into the shared student app
steps.summary: Integrate the Edge experience into the shared app home, navigation, profile, search, communications and interaction patterns. Replace Edge-specific platform functions with common Hub capabilities where these meet the need, while retaining Edge ownership of its proposition, opportunity content, curation, developmental journeys and recognition rules. Continue selective improvement of Canvas, project management, evidence and badging where live use shows clear student or operational value.

steps.title: Complete the transition of Edge into a mature Hub domain
steps.summary: Operate and improve King’s Edge as one mature product domain within the Student Experience Hub. Draw primarily on shared app, data, integration, profile, communication and service capabilities, and concentrate Edge-specific development on the quality of opportunity discovery, connected developmental journeys, evidence and recognition. Progress portfolio, articulation and enhanced-record functions only where the propositions led by 2.4.3 and the necessary data foundations are sufficiently mature.
